absent: Wide note merge helper behavior and crash read primitives, note size accounting, buffer allocators, range offset assignment and total size computation are not shown.
Global vmcore state layout and lifetime for core buffers, notes buffers, range and device dump lists, mutex, open flags, disabled flag, sizes and proc operations is not shown.
Driver dump descriptor and node structures, callback contract, dump name limits and sysfs linkage are not shown.
Mount sequence table, path formatting skip semantics, namespace event sources, reference counting for namespaces and paths, and seq and splice helpers are not shown.
Ramfs non paged mapping preparation, area allocation, attribute setter and generic file and attribute helpers are not shown.
Architecture crash header allocators, usability predicate, arch checks, range allocators and security option hook behavior are not shown.
Error handling for concurrent device dump addition versus teardown and for mount view polling races beyond generation comparison is not shown.

findings.text: Device dump registration and overall vmcore teardown are the externally reachable services in this fragment set, one accepting driver supplied dump descriptors and one releasing proc entry plus all retained ranges buffers and dumps.

Three file operation vectors provide the user visible mounts, mountinfo and mountstats views, each binding its own open routine while sharing sequential read, splice, seek and release behavior, with poll present only on the first two.

In memory filesystem regular file handling for paged builds exposes a file vector centered on generic read write and mmap preparation plus no operation sync and splice helpers, alongside an inode vector for simple attribute get and set.

In memory filesystem regular file handling for non paged builds exposes a distinct file vector centered on non paged mmap preparation and area allocation plus generic read write and splice helpers, alongside an inode vector using a non paged attribute setter.

Crash image headers are accepted only when magic matches, type indicates core, architecture check passes, class and version match the expected width and current version, header and program entry sizes equal the in memory structure sizes, and program count is nonzero, otherwise a warning is emitted and parsing fails.

Top level crash parsing first reads the identification bytes, rejects images without correct magic, then dispatches to the wide or narrow parser according to class and finally derives total vmcore size from header, notes and range list sizes.

All note segments for narrow images are coalesced into a single leading note program entry with zero flags and zero addresses and alignment four, whose file position follows the compacted header table on a page boundary and whose file and memory extents equal the summed note payload, while surplus entries are removed, tail bytes cleared, total rounded to a page, program count adjusted and original note extent remembered.

Note payload copying walks every program entry, ignores non note entries, reads each note payload from its recorded file position into successive output positions sized by its memory extent, and propagates the first read failure while returning success when no note or all notes succeed.

Load entries in both widths have their recorded positions expanded outward to page boundaries, the expanded extent registered in the vmcore range list, and their file positions rewritten to follow headers plus notes while preserving the original intra page displacement, with allocation failure aborting the walk.

Each device dump note header records name length covering the name field, descriptor length covering dump name plus payload, a device dump note type, and padded copies of the fixed note name and driver supplied dump name.

Adding device dump capacity grows a cumulative device total, recomputes notes size as rounded original notes plus that total, refreshes program entries and range offsets, and publishes the new total in both global size and proc entry size.

Program refresh after device dumps enlarges the note entry to original plus device total for both file and memory extents and reassigns every other entry file position sequentially from the end of headers plus notes while preserving intra page offsets over page expanded extents, with separate handling for each ELF width.

Boot initialization allocates architecture crash header storage, proceeds only when usable, parses headers, releases the temporary header address and marks it erroneous, then creates a read only owner proc entry sized to the computed dump; cleanup removes that entry when present and frees ranges, core buffers and device dumps.

Polling a mounts view always reports readability, registers the namespace wait queue, and additionally reports error and priority only on first observation of a new namespace event generation, which is then remembered in the sequential file state.

Superblock option display emits spellings for synchronous, directory synchronous, mandatory locking and lazy time according to superblock flags before delegating to a security hook, while mount option display emits spellings for no suid, no device, no execution, no access time, no directory access time, relative time and no symlink follow according to mount flags plus an extra marker when the mount is identity mapped.

The three mount views share helpers for escaped names and filesystem type with optional subtype, but differ in line shape: one uses device, path, type, access mode, options and fixed trailing counters; one uses identifiers, device numbers, two paths, access mode, mount options, propagation tags, separator, type, source and superblock state; one uses descriptive words around device, mountpoint, filesystem type and optional statistics.

Opening any mount view resolves the target task, takes a counted reference on its mount namespace and a copy of its filesystem root under task protection, opens private sequential state, seeds the poll generation from the namespace, and stores namespace, root and the view specific display routine; release drops root and namespace references and frees private state.
Path and name escaping for mount displays uses octal escapes for characters that would confuse parsing, including blank, tab, newline, backslash and hash for the generic mangling helper.
Paginated ramfs leaves unmapped area selection to the generic memory manager primitive, passing through file, address, length, offset and flags unchanged.
Non paged ramfs advertises direct and copy mappings together with read, write and execute permissions as its mapping capabilities.

Device dump list mutation and size publication hold the vmcore mutex across the whole commit, and device dump teardown holds the same mutex across the whole drain, so list membership and accounting cannot interleave.
Mount namespace and filesystem root capture for mount views occur while holding target task protection, ensuring the namespace pointer and root remain stable across reference acquisition.
Option mapping entries pair an integer flag mask with a pointer to a constant display spelling, terminated by a zero flag entry.
Mount view operation tables arrange open, sequential read iteration, splice read, sequential seek, release and optionally poll slots in the standard file operations layout.
Ramfs file vectors arrange read, write, mmap preparation, sync, splice and seek plus area or capability hooks, while inode vectors pair attribute set and get slots.

Crash header bringup moves from architecture allocation through usability gating to identification check, width specific validation and header fetch, note coalescing, load extent registration, offset assignment and total size publication, with any failure diverting to buffer release.

Device dump registration moves from disabled and argument checks through node and page rounded buffer allocation, header fill and driver callback, to a guarded commit that warns on late addition after first open, refuses when currently open, otherwise queues the dump and republishes sizes; failures release allocated storage.
Boot time vmcore initialization is the sole creation path for the vmcore proc entry and its backing header, notes and range state.
Each mount view file open dispatches through a dedicated entry that selects the appropriate line formatter before entering shared namespace and root capture logic.

Callers must handle invalid argument with EINVAL for malformed headers or missing dump fields or disabled dumps, memory exhaustion with ENOMEM for header or notes or range or node or buffer allocation, busy refusal with EBUSY when adding dumps while vmcore is open, and missing task or namespace or filesystem root with EINVAL or ENOENT during mount view open.

Adding device dumps after the vmcore file has ever been opened emits a one time warning about unexpected timing, and attempts while the disabled flag is set are rejected with an error and a one time diagnostic.

Mount entries whose mountpoint lies outside the viewer root produce a skip indication from path formatting and abort that line, so readers must tolerate absent entries rather than assuming complete enumeration.

Crash parsing distinguishes program kinds using PT_NOTE for notes and PT_LOAD for loads, requires file type ET_CORE, accepts width ELFCLASS64 in one parser and width ELFCLASS32 in the other, requires version EV_CURRENT in both identification and header fields, checks magic ELFMAG over SELFMAG length and identification slots EI_CLASS plus EI_VERSION, and compares header sizes against in memory header structures.

Device dumps use dedicated note type NT_VMCOREDD with fixed name VMCOREDD_NOTE_NAME, size accounting with PAGE_SIZE granularity and small note alignment, cumulative totals in dedicated size variables, and a vmcore proc entry created with mode S_IRUSR.

Mount rendering interprets superblock flags SB_SYNCHRONOUS for sync plus SB_DIRSYNC for dirsync plus SB_MANDLOCK for mand plus SB_LAZYTIME for lazytime, mount flags MNT_NOSUID plus MNT_NODEV plus MNT_NOEXEC plus MNT_NOATIME plus MNT_NODIRATIME plus MNT_RELATIME plus MNT_NOSYMFOLLOW plus MNT_READONLY for access state, propagation roles IS_MNT_SHARED plus IS_MNT_SLAVE plus IS_MNT_UNBINDABLE, poll masks EPOLLIN plus EPOLLRDNORM for readability and EPOLLERR plus EPOLLPRI for change, and device major plus minor decomposition.
